articles.title: Rethinking the Operating System: Why We Need to Explore a Synergetic Approach to Computing
articles.excerpt: Introduction: What If We Thought Differently About Operating Systems? We open a web browser, listen to music, edit documents, watch videos, download files, and communicate with people around the world…
articles.body: Introduction: What If We Thought Differently About Operating Systems? Every day, millions of people use computers without thinking about what makes them work. We open a web browser, listen to music, edit documents, watch videos, download files, and communicate with people around the world. Sometimes we do several of these things at the same time.Behind the scenes, however, a complex system is working continuously to coordinate the activities of the computer. It decides which tasks receive processing time, how memory is used, how applications access files, and how different programs share limited resources. This system is called an operating system. Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and other operating systems perform this essential role.
articles.author: Synergetic Operating System

articles.body: EverWind's October 16 announcement for Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, includes a useful cooling detail for AI infrastructure buyers: a sealed coolant circuit can coexist with water demand elsewhere in the cooling system. The developer's release targets an initial 95 MW phase for late 2027, with further expansion subject to conditions. EverWind plans a sealed water-glycol loop, with heat removed mainly through air and water-assisted cooling during the hottest weather. Under current design assumptions, it expects approximately 100,000 litres of daily water use for the initial phase and approximately 500,000 litres per day on average at full development. These are design estimates for a planned facility. They are not operating measurements.

articles.title: Application Performance Monitoring: Common Pitfalls to Avoid
articles.excerpt: Application performance monitoring (APM) gives development and operations teams a clearer view of how an application behaves in production. It helps them spot slowdowns, track down bottlenecks, and in…
articles.body: Application performance monitoring (APM) gives development and operations teams a clearer view of how an application behaves in production. It helps them spot slowdowns, track down bottlenecks, and investigate failures before they turn into serious problems for users. But simply collecting performance data does not automatically make an application more reliable. When monitoring is poorly configured, it can flood teams with alerts, hide the problems that actually matter, push up infrastructure costs, and leave important parts of the application in the dark. A team can have dashboards packed with metrics and still struggle to explain why an API suddenly became slow or why the checkout process keeps failing.
articles.author: Prerna Sharma

articles.title: TypeScript 7 Native Port, Perplexity Decision Models, and the Vercel Platform Expansion
articles.excerpt: This week's AI tooling news split cleanly between two themes: speed and consolidation. TypeScript's native port landed with build time numbers that sound made-up until you run them yourself, while Ver…
articles.body: This week's AI tooling news split cleanly between two themes: speed and consolidation. TypeScript's native port landed with build time numbers that sound made-up until you run them yourself, while Vercel quietly became a serious backend platform—and seeded it with free model access to pull developers in. Here's what's worth your attention and what to actually do with it. TypeScript 7 Native Port Delivers 8–12x Build Speedups The TypeScript team rewrote the compiler in Go. Not a binding, not a wrapper—a full port. The result is multithreaded, native-speed compilation that drops full-build times from minutes to seconds on large codebases and makes editor diagnostics (find-all-references, autocomplete, inline errors) feel near-instant.

articles.title: The Server Was Up. It Was Also Compromised.
articles.excerpt: The sites were still loading. Forms worked, pages opened, nothing was throwing errors. From the outside, everything looked fine. It wasn't. Someone else had been living on that server. A rootkit hidin…
articles.body: The sites were still loading. Forms worked, pages opened, nothing was throwing errors. From the outside, everything looked fine. It wasn't. Someone else had been living on that server. What I found A rootkit hiding processes from the usual tools Backdoor files planted in web directories, made to look like ordinary PHP files An SSH key I had never added , sitting in an authorized_keys file Cron jobs quietly running malicious scripts on a schedule None of it broke anything. That was the point. Attackers who break things get noticed and kicked out. Attackers who stay quiet keep access for months. Cleaning it up I removed the backdoors, the unknown key and every cron job I couldn't explain, got rid of the rootkit, and audited the installed packages for changed files.
articles.author: Jabed Hossain

articles.title: Docker health checks that catch real problems, explained simply
articles.excerpt: A plain guide to Docker health checks for your app, Postgres (pg_isready) and Redis, and three mistakes that make a check pass when it shouldn't. Your app starts, tries to reach the database, and cras…
articles.body: A plain guide to Docker health checks for your app, Postgres (pg_isready) and Redis, and three mistakes that make a check pass when it shouldn't. Your app starts, tries to reach the database, and crashes because Postgres is still waking up. Or worse: everything looks "healthy", but Redis is rejecting every request because of a password typo. A health check is a small command that answers one question, over and over: is this service actually ready to do its job? Get it right and you can see when a service is truly ready, broken ones are easy to spot, and your users stop seeing errors during deploys. In this guide you'll add working health checks to a web app, Postgres and Redis, deploy them as one stack, and learn the three mistakes that make a health check say "all good" when it isn't.
articles.author: octave Nkurunziza

articles.title: Motherboard VRM Explained: Power Delivery, Phases, and Cooling
articles.excerpt: When building a PC, it is easy to focus on the CPU, GPU, and RAM. But motherboard power delivery also deserves attention. One important part of this system is the VRM, or Voltage Regulator Module. It…
articles.body: When building a PC, it is easy to focus on the CPU, GPU, and RAM. But motherboard power delivery also deserves attention. One important part of this system is the VRM, or Voltage Regulator Module. It helps deliver the controlled voltage that a CPU needs to operate reliably. Understanding how it works can help you choose a suitable motherboard and avoid paying extra for specifications you may not need. What Does a Motherboard VRM Do? A motherboard VRM regulates the power supplied to the CPU. The power supply provides power to the motherboard, while the VRM converts and regulates it for the processor. The CPU's power demands change depending on its workload. Gaming, rendering, and other demanding tasks can increase power consumption.

articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.title: Tom Cruise's 10/10 War Action Epic Is About to Say Goodbye to HBO Max
articles.excerpt: Before it leaves HBO, revisit one of Tom Cruise’s richest and most emotionally resonant character studies.
articles.body: Tom Cruise has built a career out of playing larger-than-life characters, but some of his best performances are when he delves into the more vulnerable people beneath the movie-star bravado. Days of Thunder filters the story of a hotshot NASCAR driver through the humbling process of learning to trust someone, while Jerry Maguire finds a sports agent in the throes of learning that success means little without genuine human connection. Even Tropic Thunder , for all its outrageous comedy, gives Cruise room to disappear into a grotesque Hollywood executive whose insecurities are as ridiculous as his explosive temper. And Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Digger gives Cruise one of his most fascinating character studies yet as an oil tycoon with a brazen plan to save the world.

The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.
articles.author: Sharmila Kuthunur

articles.title: 10 best places to see the 2027 total solar eclipse in Spain
articles.excerpt: From the Costa del Sol to whitewashed mountain villages, here are 10 of the best places in southern Spain to experience the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse.
articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.
